big_case.notes: Plenary review on a recurring federal securities-law issue under Section 11(a) of the Securities Act of 1933 governing mid-quarter IPO disclosures across U.S. capital markets, following Omnicare and Macquarie and drawing SG/SEC participation and major financial-industry amici, but narrowed to the reformulated misleading-omissions question (excluding Item 303) and statutory-technical rather than constitutional or broad public-policy in scope.

central_claims.basis: The November 13, 2026 order granted certiorari limited to the Solicitor General's reformulated Question 1, omitted the Item 303 question, and set the case for plenary review (disposition_route 'plenary').
central_claims.claim: The Court will grant certiorari limited to Question 1, reformulated along the lines proposed by the Solicitor General, decline the broader Item 303 question, and set the case for plenary briefing and argument.

central_claims.basis: The November 13, 2026 order adopted the Solicitor General's formulation verbatim ('without an additional inquiry to determine whether the omission rendered any affirmative statement misleading').
central_claims.claim: The granted question will ask whether an issuer may be held liable under Section 11(a)'s misleading-omissions clause based on a finding that undisclosed interim financial information was material, without a separate determination that the omission rendered an affirmative statement misleading.
